The latest stable release of Next.js on GitHub is **v16.4.2**. It is tagged "Latest" on the releases page and was released on October 15, 2026 (v16.4.2 Latest). npm also lists 16.4.2 as the `latest` tag ([npm listing](https://www.npmjs.com/package/next?activeTab=versions)).

Other recent releases:
- **v16.5.0-canary.15** is the newest pre-release, dated October 15. It's a canary build, so it's not for production (index 1-3).
- **v15.5.28** came out on October 14 for the 15.x line (index 1-27).
- **v16.4.1** was also released on October 14 (index 1-23).

The Next.js blog lists an October 14, 2026 out-of-band security update for upstream vulnerabilities (index 2-4). I didn't confirm which versions that update covers.

content.text:
The latest stable Next.js is **16.4.2**, released on **October 15, 2026**. I got that from the GitHub releases page, where it's tagged "Latest". npm also lists it as the `latest` tag. I only saw search snippets, not the pages themselves, so run `npm show next version` if you need to be certain.

- **Older results:** One search returned 16.2.10 (July 2026) as the latest stable. Those sources are older than the GitHub and npm listings, so I treated them as stale.
- **Other recent releases:** v16.4.1 came out on October 14, and v16.5.0-canary.15 is a pre-release, so not for production.
- **Version 15:** The 15.x line is in maintenance, with 15.5.28 released on October 14. A lifecycle page lists its end of life as October 21, 2026.
- **Security update:** The Next.js blog mentions an out-of-band security update on October 14. I didn't confirm which versions it covers, so check the blog before you upgrade or stay put.
